reason: The giant and distant icy bodies directly match the goal of following where the old ice goes.
expectation: The giant may redirect some icy bodies inward, though their exact destination is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: This could address the leftover debris goal, but I want to follow the ice first.

effect: The giant sent a population of icy bodies inward, opening several possible encounters in warmer regions.
reaction: The separate possible fates of the scattered bodies make me curious.
reason: Following the ice into warm space seems like a direct next step toward its fate.
expectation: Some ice may turn to gas and carry dust away, as in the earlier warm-disk passage.

alternatives.reason: The icy bodies might strike rocky worlds, but I want to follow their warming first.

effect: The inward ice releases gas and dust in warm space while a cold remnant can survive.
reaction: The immense, thin cloud trailing a small remnant is a striking image.
reason: I want to follow another possible fate of the scattered icy bodies: an encounter with the rocky worlds.
expectation: Some icy bodies may strike a rocky world, though the outcome is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Collisions with debris are another possible fate, but the worlds seem more directly consequential.

effect: Some scattered ice struck the rocky worlds, completing the ice goal; the remaining goal concerns debris.
reaction: The clarification that impacts do not guarantee an ocean is useful.
reason: I want to follow what happens to leftover debris near the giant.
expectation: The giant may scatter some debris onto different paths, though its fate is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Warming the debris might reveal another fate, but I want to try the giant's influence first.

effect: The debris struck the giant's rings and produced an icy spray; the remaining offered action follows debris in warm space.
reaction: The ring impact was unexpected; I had anticipated scattering instead.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may resolve what happens to the remaining debris.
expectation: The debris may be altered or dispersed in warm space, though I am unsure how.

effect: Collisions ground some leftover stones into fine dust, opening a combination with material released from warming ice.
reaction: The debris breaking down makes physical sense.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it brings the two sources of dust together.
expectation: The rocky dust and material from the ice may mix between the worlds, though the precise result is uncertain.

effect: The rocky and icy grains mingle and scatter starlight, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The faint glow is a satisfying way to connect the two debris paths.

mostWorthwhile.text: Bringing the two dust sources together was most worthwhile: their separate histories produce a visible glow between the worlds.

leastWorthwhile.text: Grinding the leftover stones into dust felt relatively routine, especially as it was the only offered combination.

surprise.text: I expected the giant to scatter the debris, but it instead struck the rings and raised an icy spray.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt clearly purposeless, although the final dust combination was the only offered action rather than a meaningful choice.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to follow the system further; the different fates of its ice and debris made the chapter engaging.
